correctness.rationale: For one/two update images, labeled de Bruijn graphs have 4/16 vertices encoding length-3/5 input windows. A finite output word is present iff a corresponding labeled path exists, because every finite input block extends to a bilateral configuration. Subset transitions from all vertices recognize exactly both image languages. Paired-subset BFS over the finite reachable graph either returns a provably shortest accepted-at-one/rejected-at-two word or exhausts states proving equality for every finite word and hence closed subshift equality; no unbounded experiment is inferred from a cutoff. A fresh independent implementation of all 256 rules reproduced 72 stable, 184 shrinking, the entire twelve-length histogram, two extremizers and max 252 reached subset pairs. The supplied classification.csv agrees with this independently computed result.
residual_risks: Comparison only first and second images, not every later shrinking step.
Bilateral full shift, binary radius-one CA; no boundary convention of finite periodic rings.
Graph-construction methods and Rule126 one/two-step graphs are prior art.
